study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: The aim of this work was to establish novel normative models of thalamic nuclear volumes and their laterality indices and investigate their changes in SCZ and AD.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: The paper explicitly describes two different strategies for handling site effects depending on the model type (univariate vs. multivariate). For univariate models, site effects were mitigated with ComBat (implemented in NeuroHarmonize), with effects estimated from controls and applied to all. For multivariate models, site was included as a random effect covariate in the GAMLSS model.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between z-scores and clinical variables (MMSE, MoCA, amyloid-tau index, PSYRATS, SAPS/SANS, PANSS), with Benjamini-Hochberg for multiple testing correction. z-score distributions between groups were compared with the z-test. Counts of extreme z-score deviations were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: In AD, thalamic nuclei are severely and symmetrically affected, while in SCZ, right-sided thalamic nuclei, particularly the right medial dorsal nucleus, are more affected and associated with symptoms.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study observed progressive volume reduction in thalamic nuclei from EMCI to AD, most severely affecting the bilateral AV, MD/Pf, and Pul nuclei, which correlated with clinical measures. In schizophrenia (SCZ), results were more heterogeneous but showed a clear predilection for right-sided thalamic atrophy, especially in the right AV, VA, VLa, and MD/Pf nuclei. The right MD/Pf nucleus z-scores were associated with thought disorder and hallucinations in SCZ. The normative modeling approach identified more significant changes than traditional case-control analysis.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Relatively small number of individuals in the SCZ cohorts; moderate sample size for normative modeling; absence of some thalamic nuclei in the analyses; using the same model for all regions; interpretation of volume change as functional change is indirect; small size of some nuclei (LGN, MGN) makes them susceptible to noise; potential confounding from disease duration, substance abuse, medication, and head motion were not analyzed.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Weaknesses of the current study include a relatively small number of individuals in the SCZ cohorts, a moderate sample size for normative modeling, absence of some thalamic nuclei such as the centrolateral or intralaminar nuclei in the analyses, and using the same model for all regions. ... Our interpretation of volumetric changes is dependent on a change in volume being associated with a change in network function without assessing the network directly. ... Some regions such as the LGN and MGN are small and potentially more susceptible to subtle variability and imaging artifacts despite their accurate segmentation. ... Finally, relevant factors such as disease duration, substance abuse, medication burden, and head motion that may confound results were outside the scope of these analyses.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study developed and applied novel normative models for laterality index (LI) in addition to regional volumes. The study also performed a direct comparison between the normative modeling approach and a traditional case-control (ANCOVA) analysis, finding that normative modeling identified more affected regions.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study presents novel normative models for thalamic nuclei volumes and, for the first time, their laterality indices (LI). It leverages a new, more accurate segmentation method (HIPS-THOMAS) for T1 images. The models were built on a large, aggregated dataset of 2,374 healthy controls spanning ages 5.6 to 100. The full list of cohorts used for the reference group are: HCP DEV, HCP EP, HCP YA, UCLA, SCZ AH, HCP AGE, and ADNI.
